Asymmetric C atalysis
Enantio- and Diastereoselective Synthesis of Chiral Tetrasubstituted
α-Amino Allenoates Bearing a Vicinal All-Carbon Quaternary
Stereocenter with Dual-Copper-Catalysis
Cheng Sheng
+
, Zheng Ling
+
, Junzhe Xiao, Kai Yang, Fang Xie, Shengming Ma,* and
Wanbin Zhang*
Abstract: The skeletons of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes
bearing a vicinal all-carbon quaternary stereocenter are
of importance but still challenging to synthesize. Herein,
we report enantio- and diastereoselective γ-additions of
1-alkynyl ketimines with dual-copper-catalysis under
mild conditions, affording chiral tetrasubstituted α-
amino allenoates bearing a vicinal all-carbon quaternary
stereocenter in high yields (up to 99 % yield) with
excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99 % ee) and diaster-
eoselectivities (up to > 20 : 1 dr). Importantly, the stereo-
divergent synthesis of the products was realized by the
asymmetric γ-addition reaction and the Grignard re-
agent promoted epimerization. Moreover, the dual-
copper-catalyzed γ-addition reactions were smoothly
applied to a gram-scale reaction and adopted to
introduce chiral tetrasubstituted allenyl moieties into
bioactive molecules. Mechanistic experiments and den-
sity functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated
that the asymmetric γ-addition reactions were catalyzed
by double chiral copper catalysts.
Introduction
Chirality is one of the elemental natures of substances,
producing a world of diversity. For example, allene-based
axial chirality and carbon-based central chirality are wide-
spread in natural products and pharmaceuticals.
[1, 2]
Com-
pared with molecules containing a single type of chirality,
compounds possessing both axial and central chiralities,
particularly chiral allenes bearing a vicinal stereocenter
including chiral tetrasubstituted allenes with a vicinal all-
carbon quaternary center, have not attracted much atten-
tion, although they are also found in numerous bioactive
molecules and represent one of the most significant catego-
ries (Figure 1).
[1, 3]
Over the past decade, a variety of
methods for the synthesis of optically axial chiral allenes
bearing a vicinal stereocenter have been reported
successively.
[4–6]
However, because the construction of a
single chiral tetrasubstituted allene or all-carbon substituted
quaternary center remains challenging,
[7–9]
the asymmetric
synthesis of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes with a vicinal all-
carbon quaternary center are much more challenging to
forge and the asymmetric synthetic methods are still in
infancy due to their increasing structural congestion and
chiral complexity (Scheme 1a).

1-Alkynyl ketimines are important synthons containing
multi active sites (α, β and γ).
[11]
The γ-selective addition of
this type of substrates will afford allenamines, which has
attracted great attention for their considerable antiretroviral
activities and synthetic applications.
[1b, 12]
Based on previous
work concerning dual-metal-catalysis,
[13, 14]
we envisioned a
concept of asymmetric γ-additions of 1-alkynyl ketimines to
synthesize tetrasubstituted allenes with a vicinal all-carbon
quaternary stereocenter using dual-metal-catalysis, in which
M
2

repulsion with M
1
-ligand-activated imine unit to prevent the
α-additions (Scheme 1b, top). In the realized catalytic
protocol, readily available α-substituted cyanoacetates are
applying as the nucleophiles for the successful generation of
both the fully loaded axial allene and vicinal acyclic all-
carbon quaternary stereocenter using dual-metal-catalysis
with the same copper catalyst (Scheme 1b, bottom).
Results and Discussion
Based on the above hypothesis of dual-metal-catalysis, our
study commenced with the investigation of several combina-
tions of transition metal catalysts. Considering the effica-
cious catalytic outcome of copper salts in the asymmetric
addition reactions of 1-alkynyl ketimines,
[11d]
we selected
Cu(OAc)
2
as the catalyst to control ketimine substrate 1 a
and several other transition metal salts to chelate α-
substituted cyanoacetate 2 (Table 1, entries 1–3). To our
delight, by using bis(oxazoline) (BOX) L1 as the ligand, all
the reactions afforded high γ-selectivities. Subsequently, the
inspection of different single metal salts indicated that the
reaction catalyzed by Cu(OAc)
2

substituted cyanoacetate compared with other metal salts

optimized using copper as the metal salt. Nucleophiles with
ethyl, benzyl and tert-butyl ester groups were then tested

tert-butyl ester group was able to give the γ-addition product
in 91 % yield with higher stereoselectivity (entry 10). Grati-

asymmetric γ-addition reactions proceeded completely at

gram-scale synthesis of 3 aa was conducted (Scheme 2a). To
our delight, the resulting product was afforded in quantita-
tive yield with excellent stereoselectivity. The stereodiver-
gent synthesis of molecules is meaningful since the absolute
and relative configurations are influential for their biological
activities in many cases. However, to the best of our
knowledge, there have been no reports concerning the
stereodivergent synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenes bearing
a vicinal all-carbon quaternary center. Intriguingly, we found
that an equivalent of MeMgBr could be employed as a base
to deprotonate the carbamate NH group of 3 aa and
facilitate the epimerization of 3 aa, which was an effective

details, see Supporting Information). Thus, all four stereo-

To study the mechanism of this copper-catalyzed asym-
metric γ-addition reaction, a series of control experiments

catalysis system might not be involved in a radical process
(for details, see Supporting Information). Then, substrates
1 aa (R = Ph) and 1 ab (R = CF

reaction. In addition, during the solvent screening process, it

only afforded the α-addition product rather than the desired
γ-addition product (for details, see Supporting Information).

C onclusion
In conclusion, we have demonstrated an asymmetric γ-
addition reaction of α-substituted cyanoacetates to 1-alkynyl
ketimines with dual-copper-catalysis which was successfully
applied to synthesize chiral tetrasubstituted α-amino alle-
noates bearing a vicinal all-carbon quaternary stereocenter
in high yields and with excellent stereoselectivities (up to
99 % yield, 99 % ee and > 20 : 1 dr). Mechanism studies
revealed that the asymmetric γ-addition reactions are
catalyzed by double chiral Cu catalysts. The asymmetric
catalytic reaction was carried out smoothly on a gram scale
and the stereodivergent synthesis of this type of compounds
was firstly realized. In addition, the catalytic system was
efficiently applied to introduce chiral tetrasubstituted allenes
and all-carbon quaternary stereocenters into bioactive
molecules. The allene-based axial chirality was transformed
to central chirality and formed a significant type of
oxazolone derivative.
